source.title: Understanding training and generalization in deep learning by Fourier analysis

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests how initialization scale and frequency learning relate to held-out generalization, using different measures and settings from the listed versions. Its findings fit none of V1–V8.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses prior findings about random-label memorization, but reports no random-label experiment. Figure descriptions provide qualitative outcomes; exact plotted values are not stated.
record.test_reason: The study tests initialization scale and frequency-learning dynamics, which fit none of V1–V8. It discusses random-label memorization and flat minima, but reports neither a natural-versus-random-label experiment nor magnitude-scaled perturbation measurements. Using Adam alone does not test V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors argue that small weight initialization favors lower-frequency, lower-complexity fitted functions and better generalization when the training data capture the target's important frequencies. They demonstrate initialization effects on a natural image and MNIST, argue that weights matter more than biases, and acknowledge that their framework does not resolve architectural or width-versus-depth differences. Their arbitrary-function capacity claim is theoretical, not a reported random-label experiment.
record.recipe_differences: Uses tanh networks trained with Adam and mean squared error; studies initialization and Fourier behavior rather than the original sources' interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization scale changes held-out generalization; the paper reports a smaller effect from bias initialization than from weight initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: Small initialization yields similar training and held-out pixel errors; larger initialization fits training pixels but produces noisy held-out predictions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization scale affects generalization in the tested tanh network reconstructing a natural image.

fits_no_version.finding: MNIST test accuracy is much higher with weight initialization standard deviation 0.01 than 0.3. Raising bias initialization standard deviation to 2.5 with small weights produces a smaller deterioration.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight initialization scale affects generalization more strongly than bias initialization scale in the tested MNIST setup.

fits_no_version.finding: The discussion qualitatively associates smaller weights with smaller loss curvature and better generalization, without measuring magnitude-aware sharpness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The Fourier framework suggests an association between initialization scale, unnormalized loss curvature, and generalization.

record.problems: The generalization experiments use particular tanh DNNs and datasets. Exact test errors and accuracies are shown only in figures and are not stated in the text. The paper says its framework does not analyze detailed effects of network structure or width and depth.
record.rows_left_out: No additional standalone results bearing on the listed versions were reported. Frequency-convergence descriptions and theoretical results concern frequency-learning behavior, not one of V1–V8.

untested.parts: Joint demonstration of random-label fitting capacity, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance held-out accuracy under random labels using the same architecture and recipe.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer comparisons and effects of tuning, weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects under matched epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out performance across data sizes, dropout strengths, or augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because every row fits none of those versions; this does not dispute the reported initialization effects. No missing result establishes a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural versus random labels.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of tuning or optimizer changes.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout and its effects with different training-set sizes or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.
